item.title: After commercial whaling nearly erased them, blue and fin whales are slowly reclaiming the southeast Atlantic
item.description: More than 40 years after the end of commercial whaling, new research reveals a recent increase in sightings of the world's two largest whale species in the southeastern Atlantic. The findings, published in the African Journal of Marine Science, compiled more than 60 years of confirmed sightings and strandings from Namibia and South Africa's west coast. Although overall numbers remain low, sightings of both species have increased markedly in recent years—with 95% of observations recorded since 2012. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Cells pulse together as they grow—and malignant cells pulse the longest
item.description: Epithelial cells are the tiny shields that line and protect our bodies. In a developing embryo, epithelial cells grow, divide and move into positions to form the outer layers of our skin and the surfaces of our organs and blood vessels. When we scrape our skin, suffer an internal tear or undergo surgery, epithelial cells migrate to the site of injury to heal a wound. And when epithelial cells go haywire, they can turn malignant and spread through the body as cancer. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.description: Years after civil war drove many Muslims from Sibut, the call to prayer is echoing again from the town’s rebuilt central mosque. item.title: Brunei Sultan strips daughter-in-law’s royal title; no divorce yet announced from Prince Abdul Malik
item.description: Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah of Brunei has stripped daughter-in-law Pengiran Raabi’atul Adawiyyah of her royal title over conduct deemed “unbecoming” of a royal spouse. item.title: El Salvador: ¿golpe contra las pandillas o a los derechos humanos?
item.description: Más de 480 presuntos integrantes de pandillas fueron juzgados de manera colectiva en El Salvador, en uno de los episodios más controvertidos del régimen de excepción impulsado por Nayib Bukele. Mientras el Gobierno defiende estas medidas como parte de su ofensiva contra el crimen organizado y reivindica la drástica reducción de la violencia, organizaciones de derechos humanos cuestionan las detenciones y los procedimientos judiciales. ¿Dónde termina la lucha contra las pandillas y comienza el riesgo de normalizar la excepción? Lo analizamos junto a expertos en El Debate de France 24. Fuente: France 24 - Español.
item.dc:creator: Andrés Meza

item.title: US could exhaust domestic phosphorus within 40 years, but waste offers reserves
item.description: The United States could exhaust its domestic phosphorus supply within 40 years. item.title: In 1870, a former slave and Union soldier staked a homestead in Nebraska
item.description: Escaping the bonds of slavery, Robert Ball Anderson became a proud soldier in the Union Army. Despite facing significant obstacles in farming caused by severe weather and pests, he dedicated himself to saving money through various jobs, including cooking for railroads. His efforts culminated in owning more than two thousand acres of fertile land, exemplifying the strength and resilience of African Americans in achieving landownership across the Great Plains. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: 208 mil reproducciones · 41 mil reacciones | It’s not about race, it’s about ethnicity. I believe everyone should be able to have communities/countries of people of their own ethnic background that are for them. Nigerians get their own community. Indians get their own community. Chinese get their own community. And that means Germanic people, Nordic people, Celtic people etc. (white European ethnicities) also get their own place. They share a common language, common religion, a common culture, common values, and a common heritage. All “race” problems would be solved in a day if we organized in this way. Why is it racist to say all these other people can have their own place to live just for them with their own people and traditions, but if I want my own with my own people it’s an ethnostate? Because my skin is white? Being “white” does not even accurately represent all of the different cultures in European history, and my Germanic ethnicity is not the same as a Turkish ethnicity for example. I should have every right to a Germanic home that is for Germanic people just as much as the Indian has India, the Albanian has Albania, the Ghanaian has Ghana, or the Japanese has Japan. I want to live with and around people who have the same language, values, culture, and religion as me, not people who I have nothing in common with. Different cultures have different beauties about them that make them unique. I enjoy visiting them and learning about them. But they are not mine, and they never will be, and I do not want them in my home. | Will Witt
